01_indian_breakfast_cereal: Ordinary case: hierarchy and raw text agree, listed for India.
02_same_kind_edited_in_french: Same product kind as 01, last edited in French. Raw categories text differs completely; categories_hierarchy (matched ids) is identical. Reading raw text loses this match.
03_raw_leaf_collision: A cereal BAR whose raw categories text ends on 'Breakfast cereals'. Reading the raw leaf invents a match with a cereal that the hierarchy does not support.
04_india_only_in_the_taxonomy: Raw countries say 'Inde'; only countries_tags carries en:india. A closed set of English spellings would miss it.
05_raw_says_india_taxonomy_does_not: Raw countries say 'India' while countries_tags do not. The raw text is editor prose and can disagree with the taxonomy.
06_no_category_hierarchy: categories_hierarchy absent. No key, so the row cannot support a comparison.
07_empty_category_hierarchy: categories_hierarchy empty. Distinct from absent and equally unusable: two unclassified products are not comparable.
08_unmatched_hierarchy_entry: A taxonomy-unmatched entry kept AS-IS in categories_hierarchy ('fr:Chikki Maison') vs deaccented/lowercased in categories_tags. Usable only as an exact match.
09_lookalike_country: en:british-indian-ocean-territory: a different country with its own id, never India.
10_malformed_hierarchy: A non-string entry in categories_hierarchy. One unreadable entry voids the whole classification rather than being dropped.
11_lossy_collision_a: Distinct source category 'fr:Müsli maison' in the non-lossy hierarchy; lossy categories_tags token 'fr:musli-maison'. Pairs with 12.
12_lossy_collision_b: Distinct source category 'fr:Musli maison' (no umlaut) in the non-lossy hierarchy; SAME lossy categories_tags token 'fr:musli-maison' as 11. Proof that categories_tags can manufacture a false match while categories_hierarchy does not.
